name: Golgari Midrange (discard, removal, one big threat)
description: A Modern-style black-green midrange curve: turn-1 discard to strip your best card, a cheap efficient threat, a planeswalker that edicts, and one-for-one removal every turn after. Teaches threat density and sequencing around discard: play the redundant piece first, keep the engine card until they have tapped out or spent the discard.

turns.boardSummary: Overgrown Tomb; Thoughtseize took your best card

events.note: Turn-1 discard: they look at your hand and take the best card. Decision point: which card would you least like to lose? That is the one to play FIRST next time you can.
events.breakPoint: You cannot stop the discard, but you can blunt it: keep two copies of the same role (two outlets, two payoffs) so losing one does not end the line.

events.note: A two-mana threat that grows with the graveyards. It will be a 4/5 by turn 4.

turns.boardSummary: 3 lands, Tarmogoyf, Liliana of the Veil (edict used)

events.note: Planeswalker: -2 makes you sacrifice a creature. An edict ignores hexproof and indestructible; it takes your worst creature only if you have more than one.
events.breakPoint: Against an edict, keep a spare body (a token or a cheap creature) on the battlefield before you deploy the engine piece.

turns.boardSummary: 4 lands, Tarmogoyf 4/5, Liliana ticking up, Fatal Push in hand

events.note: One-mana instant-speed removal for a creature with mana value 2 or less. It will target the engine piece, not the fodder.
events.breakPoint: Sacrifice the targeted creature in response if you have an outlet: the removal fizzles (no legal target, CR 608.2b) and you still get the death trigger.

turns.boardSummary: 5 lands, Tarmogoyf, Scavenging Ooze eating graveyards

events.note: Incidental graveyard hate: every green mana exiles a card from a graveyard. Recursion lines get slower from here.
events.breakPoint: Recur the piece you need NOW rather than banking value in the graveyard; anything left there will be exiled at their leisure.

turns.boardSummary: 6 lands, two attackers; you must be ahead on board or life by now

events.note: Decision point: midrange wins long games through card quality. If your line is not online by turn 6, you are the beatdown now — trade life for tempo.
